Alan Raph was born in New York City on July 3, 1933. He came from a musical family and has fashioned a successful career as a trombonist and low brass player. Alan has played for most of the major names in the classical and jazz world, including Eugene Ormandy, Villa Lobos, Quincy Jones and Gerry Mulligan. He earned a “Most Valuable Player” award from the National Association of Recording Arts & Sciences and currently sustains a multifaceted career as a performer, composer and educator.
Alan was interviewed in Danbury, Connecticut on November 20, 2001, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
